items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: The first time I heard it called Boogie-Woogie was when Pinetop Smith recorded for Mayo

ctx.x: No. The first time I heard it called Boogie-Woogie was when Pinetop Smith recorded for Mayo {Williams, 1929}* out of Chicago. But before that, that movement, that bass movement, Blind Lemon Jefferson played on his guitar. And he called it Booga-Rooga. So now I don't know how...I guess that sometimes, you know what I mean, sometimes inexplicable, how you can explain terms, descriptions falling in a certain category and becoming a certain thing, as it final result. But it was Booga-Rooga for Blind Lemon Jefferson.…
So how long did you stay with the show?
